_note: The streaming envelope (local-ai-engine.md §4.5, Appendix A7). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) a completion is a DECLARED stream action — events ride the kernel envelope {id, event, final, data} and are rid-correlated, so two jobs are told apart by the envelope and never by a hand-rolled payload id. (2) `token` events carry SEQUENCE-NUMBERED DELTAS, never the cumulative text: the cumulative-snapshot-per-token wire is O(n^2) bytes over the bridge and does not become public grammar — `maxEventBytes` fails any implementation that ships it (the bound applies to incremental events; `sync` and `complete` ARE snapshots by design and are exempt). (3) `seq` is per-request and monotonic from 0, so a late joiner knows what it missed and a resync tells it. (4) `sync` answers with the full typed-block snapshot, both when the engine schedules one and on demand. (5) `complete` is the terminal event (`final: true`) carrying the final snapshot and usage; nothing follows it on that rid. (6) cancellation settles the request typed and stops the stream — no orphaned events, no silent truncation. (7) an engine-side failure is a typed error on the same rid, never a partial success. The mock drains requests deterministically in submission order: what these cases assert is ATTRIBUTION (which rid an event belongs to), never the scheduler's interleaving.

cases.name: stream: token events carry deltas, never the cumulative snapshot
cases._note: The wire-economics fixture. Twelve eight-character tokens: a delta wire keeps every token event small and flat, a cumulative wire grows to ~120 bytes of text on the last one. The bound is asserted against incremental events only.

cases.name: stream: an on-demand resync answers with the full snapshot
cases._note: The late-joiner path: a surface that attached mid-stream asks for the state it missed and gets typed blocks, not a replay of deltas.

cases.name: stream: a scripted sync marker emits a snapshot mid-stream
cases._note: The periodic half of the resync law — the engine may schedule a snapshot without anyone asking, and it carries the same shape as the on-demand one.

cases.name: stream: thinking rides its own block type
cases._note: Reasoning models stream thought separately from answer text; a surface that renders only `text` must not concatenate them, and the final snapshot keeps both blocks distinct.

cases.name: stream: cancel settles the request typed and stops the stream
stream: an engine failure is a typed error on the same rid
cases._note: A partial stream that fails does not resolve as success and does not vanish: the request settles with a typed error carrying the engine's code, and the ledger sees it.

cases.name: stream: await mode resolves with the final snapshot and usage
cases._note: The non-streaming caller is the same request with a different settle: one awaited result, the events still available to anyone watching.
